newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: STET in alliance with AT&T.
newsitem.headline: STET in alliance with AT&T.

text.p: Italy's STET/Telecom Italia and AT&T Corp of the United States on Wednesday ended media speculation by announcing they were forging a strategic global telecoms alliance with a focus on Latin America and Europe.
"In the framework of a global strategic alliance, AT&T and STET/Telecom Italia decided to join forces to serve international customers," a joint statement said.
In Europe, STET/Telecom Italia would join the AT&T-Unisource telecoms joint venture, with the option of taking up to 30 percent of AT&T-Unisource.

Unisource, the grouping of Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT, currently owns 60 percent of pan-European business telecoms venture AT&T-Unisource, with AT&T holding the remaining 40 percent.

AT&T-Unisource offers telecoms services to businesses in Europe and globally via its membership of the WorldPartners Association. WorldPartners groups 16 telecom service providers, distributing services in over 30 countries.

STET/Telecom Italia plans to distribute AT&T-Unisource services in Italy. In return the Italian group will transfer into AT&T-Unisource the relevant business activities of data and telecoms unit Telemedia International (TMI).
In Latin America, STET/Telecom Italia and AT&T will form a 50-50 percent joint venture that will deliver a portfolio of global services.
AT&T Corp president and chief operating officer told Reuters it was too early to talk about the U.S. company taking a stake in STET, up for privatisation by Italy in the autumn.
STET's statutes envisage a maximum three percent stake for private shareholders with the possibility of five percent with Treasury approval.
"I think it's premature at this particular point to speculate on that. The Italian government has yet to define specifics associated with the privatisation," he said in a telephone interview.
Asked if AT&T wanted a stake in STET, Walter said the most important thing was that AT&T had a very strong alliance that satisfied its customers' expectations.
"That does not require an equity investment but at the same time equity investments...do create a stronger business model and it's something we're open to," Walter said.

STET/Telecom Italia announced the news in a statement issued jointly with AT&T and Netherlands-based Unisource, ending long-running media speculation about whether the U.S. and Italian groups would get together.

Such speculation had flared after Telefonica of Spain was asked to leave Unisource NV in April after forming an alliance with AT&T rival Concert, the British Telecom Plc /MCI Communications Corp partnership.
Telefonica's move had raised questions about AT&T- Unisource's ability to compete globally with Concert and Global One, the venture grouping Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom.
"It's something that was expected, it was a logical step. AT&T's found a replacement for Telefonica," said one telecoms analyst, declining to be named.
"Telefonica has been flavour of the month because they have a very strong presence in Latin America, STET has some clout there but nowhere near that of Telefonica," said another.
The Italian group's Latin American venture with AT&T will deliver a portfolio of global services via two newly formed pan-American operating entities, the statement said.

One will serve multinational customers, large and medium-sized businesses, and high-end consumers throughout the region. The other will offer telecoms transport services to the region's telecommunications providers.

"The alliance between STET/Telecom Italia and AT&T is based on the complementary expertise and strong local presence of the two partners and their affiliates in Latin America," the statement, issued in the Netherlands, said.

Walter said AT&T was delighted to have STET/Telecom Italia as a strategic partner. "Our businesses are highly complementary in both Europe and Latin America and our vision of the future is the same," he said in the statement.

"Our link with AT&T in Latin America will allow us to grow from strength, since we already have a major presence on that continent," Stet/Telecom Italia chief executive Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano said in the statement.
"The relationship with AT&T and Unisource in Europe will help us to provide an even more competitive range of services to our customers," he added.
